headline: Spanish Conjugation Patterns Master
threshold: Practice 28 named teaching patterns across 60 lessons, with ten distinct verbs and checked forms in every lesson.

lessons.title: Preterite spelling changes · independent practice
lessons.objective: Preterite spelling changes · independent practice: In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

words.es: Al contar la historia, expliqué por qué llegué tarde.
words.en: When telling the story, I explained why I arrived late.

words.es: Esa mañana estaba lloviendo y había mucho tráfico.
words.en: That morning it was raining and there was a lot of traffic.

lessons.speaking: Use Preterite spelling changes while discussing retell a journey with causes. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing retell a journey with causes. In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation. Other persons follow regular -ar endings. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation. Other persons follow regular -ar endings.

examples.en: to look for · Preterite spelling changes
to take out · Preterite spelling changes

lessons.title: Strong irregular preterite · independent practice
lessons.objective: Strong irregular preterite · independent practice: Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents.

words.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

words.es: Siempre llevaba un libro en la mochila.
words.en: I always used to carry a book in my backpack.
That day I forgot the backpack.

words.es: Mientras esperaba el tren, compré un periódico.
words.en: While I was waiting for the train, I bought a newspaper.

words.es: El viaje fue distinto de lo habitual.
words.en: The journey was different from the usual one.

words.es: Mi compañera me preguntó dónde estaba la mochila.
words.en: My coworker asked me where the backpack was.

words.es: Le dije que la había dejado en casa.
words.en: I told her that I had left it at home.

lessons.speaking: Use Strong irregular preterite while discussing explain a change of routine. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain a change of routine. Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents. Decir uses dijeron; hacer uses hizo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents. Decir uses dijeron; hacer uses hizo.

examples.en: to be (condition / location) · Strong irregular preterite

lessons.title: Preterite -ir stem changes · independent practice
lessons.objective: Preterite -ir stem changes · independent practice: These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes.

words.es: Leía un mensaje cuando sonó el teléfono.
words.en: I was reading a message when the phone rang.

words.es: Mi hermana estaba en la puerta.
words.en: My sister was at the door.

words.es: Buscaba mis llaves cuando ella llamó otra vez.
words.en: I was looking for my keys when she called again.

words.es: Abrí la puerta y le pedí un minuto.
words.en: I opened the door and asked her for a minute.

words.es: Mientras ella esperaba, encontré las llaves.
words.en: While she was waiting, I found the keys.
We left together for the station.

words.es: Mi hermana quería saber si yo estaba listo.
words.en: My sister wanted to know whether I was ready.

words.es: Le expliqué que había perdido unos minutos buscando.
words.en: I explained that I had lost a few minutes searching.

lessons.speaking: Use Preterite -ir stem changes while discussing describe an interrupted task. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe an interrupted task. These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes. Nosotros keeps the infinitive stem. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes. Nosotros keeps the infinitive stem.

examples.en: to ask for · Preterite -ir stem changes

lessons.title: Past habits: -ar imperfect · independent practice
lessons.objective: Past habits: -ar imperfect · independent practice: Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions.

words.en: I have lived here since January.

words.es: Trabajo en la biblioteca desde hace dos meses.
words.en: I have worked at the library for two months.

words.es: Hace tres semanas conocí a mis vecinos.
words.en: I met my neighbors three weeks ago.

words.es: No veo a mi hermano desde el verano.
words.en: I have not seen my brother since the summer.
How long have you been studying Spanish?

words.es: Estudio español desde el año pasado.
words.en: I have been studying Spanish since last year.

words.es: En enero no conocía a nadie en el edificio.
words.en: In January I did not know anyone in the building.

words.es: Una vecina me invitó a tomar café.
words.en: A neighbor invited me to have coffee.

lessons.speaking: Use Past habits: -ar imperfect while discussing introduce a neighborhood over time. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing introduce a neighborhood over time. Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions. Context separates yo from él. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions. Context separates yo from él.

lessons.title: Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect · independent practice
lessons.objective: Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect · independent practice: Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions.

words.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.
Where did you put the tickets?

words.es: Los puse dentro de la mochila.
words.en: I put them inside the backpack.

words.es: Necesito el pasaporte, pero no lo encuentro.
words.en: I need the passport, but I cannot find it.

words.es: Aquí está; lo dejaste sobre la mesa.
words.en: Here it is; you left it on the table.

words.es: Mi hermana me pidió que revisara todos los bolsillos.
words.en: My sister asked me to check all the pockets.

words.es: Ya los había revisado dos veces.
words.en: I had already checked them twice.

lessons.speaking: Use Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect while discussing resolve a missing travel document. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing resolve a missing travel document. Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions. All these endings carry a written accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions. All these endings carry a written accent.

lessons.title: Future simple · independent practice
lessons.objective: Future simple · independent practice: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem.

words.es: Se lo voy a devolver esta tarde.
words.en: I am going to return it to her this afternoon.
And the photos of her children?

words.es: También se las voy a llevar.
words.en: I am also going to take them to her.

words.es: Marta me prestó el libro el lunes.
words.en: Marta lent me the book on Monday.
I want to give it to her before the trip.

words.es: Marta me preguntó si podía pasar por su oficina.
words.en: Marta asked me whether I could stop by her office.

words.es: Le dije que llevaría las fotos en una carpeta.
words.en: I told her I would bring the photos in a folder.

lessons.speaking: Use Future simple while discussing clarify a recipient and an object. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing clarify a recipient and an object. Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem. The future can predict and can express a guess. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem. The future can predict and can express a guess.

lessons.title: Conditional simple · independent practice
lessons.objective: Conditional simple · independent practice: Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem.

words.es: A mi amiga le interesa la historia.
words.en: My friend is interested in history.

words.es: Nos encanta conversar sobre los personajes.

words.en: Are you interested in our reading group?

words.es: Me gusta la idea, pero no me gustan las reuniones largas.
words.en: I like the idea, but I do not like long meetings.

words.es: Entonces te va a encantar nuestro horario.
words.en: Then you are going to love our schedule.

words.es: Una compañera propuso leer una novela larga.
words.en: A classmate suggested reading a long novel.

words.es: A mí me interesaba, pero no tenía tiempo suficiente.
words.en: I was interested, but I did not have enough time.

lessons.speaking: Use Conditional simple while discussing negotiate a group preference. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing negotiate a group preference. Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem. Use for hypothetical results and softened requests. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem. Use for hypothetical results and softened requests.

lessons.title: Present subjunctive · independent practice
lessons.objective: Present subjunctive · independent practice: After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive.

words.es: Se me cayó una taza en la cocina.
words.en: I accidentally dropped a cup in the kitchen.

words.es: La taza se rompió en el suelo.
words.en: The cup broke on the floor.

words.es: A mi hermano se le olvidó traer una toalla.
words.en: My brother forgot to bring a towel.
We cleaned up the water carefully.

words.es: Por suerte nadie se hizo daño.
Le expliqué a mi hermano que el suelo seguía mojado.
words.en: I explained to my brother that the floor was still wet.

words.es: Le pedí que no entrara hasta que terminara de limpiar.
words.en: I asked him not to enter until I finished cleaning.

lessons.speaking: Use Present subjunctive while discussing describe an accident without blame. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe an accident without blame. After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive. Start from yo present, remove o, and switch ar to e endings, er/ir to a endings; learn exceptions. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive. Start from yo present, remove o, and switch ar to e endings, er/ir to a endings; learn exceptions.

lessons.title: Imperfect subjunctive: -ra · independent practice
lessons.objective: Imperfect subjunctive: -ra · independent practice: Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel.

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

words.es: El alquiler es tan caro como el anterior.
words.en: The rent is as expensive as the previous one.

words.es: Este es el edificio más tranquilo de la calle.
words.en: This is the quietest building on the street.

words.es: Para mí, la ubicación es la mejor ventaja.
words.en: For me, the location is the best advantage.

words.es: Tenemos que comparar también los gastos.
words.en: We also need to compare the expenses.

words.es: El dueño nos explicó qué gastos estaban incluidos.
words.en: The owner explained which expenses were included.

words.es: El otro apartamento tenía un alquiler más bajo.
words.en: The other apartment had lower rent.

lessons.speaking: Use Imperfect subjunctive: -ra while discussing defend an apartment choice. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing defend an apartment choice. Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel. Used after past wishes and in si hypotheses. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel. Used after past wishes and in si hypotheses.

lessons.title: Affirmative tú commands · independent practice
lessons.objective: Affirmative tú commands · independent practice: For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form.

words.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
words.en: This package is for my sister.

words.es: Compré una caja para proteger el regalo.
words.en: I bought a box to protect the gift.

words.es: Pasé por la oficina de correos.
words.en: I went by the post office.

words.es: Pagué diez euros por el envío.
words.en: I paid ten euros for the shipping.

words.es: Gracias por ayudarme con la dirección.
words.en: Thank you for helping me with the address.

words.es: El empleado notó que faltaba el número del apartamento.
words.en: The employee noticed that the apartment number was missing.

words.es: Me pidió que lo escribiera en otra etiqueta.
words.en: He asked me to write it on another label.

lessons.speaking: Use Affirmative tú commands while discussing correct a shipping error. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing correct a shipping error. For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form. Memorize di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven; this bank practices those eight plus two regular verbs. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form. Memorize di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven; this bank practices those eight plus two regular verbs.

examples.en: to say / tell · Affirmative tú commands
to do / make · Affirmative tú commands

lessons.title: Negative tú commands · independent practice
lessons.objective: Negative tú commands · independent practice: Use no plus the tú present subjunctive.

words.es: No hay nadie en la oficina.
words.en: There is nobody in the office.
I did not find any new message.
Do you have any news from the director?
No, I still do not know anything.

words.es: Nunca cerramos tan temprano los lunes.
words.en: We never close this early on Mondays.

words.es: Decidí no dejar un mensaje con datos privados.
words.en: I decided not to leave a message with private details.

words.es: Un compañero encontró un aviso en la puerta lateral.
words.en: A coworker found a notice on the side door.

lessons.speaking: Use Negative tú commands while discussing verify information from a notice. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing verify information from a notice. Use no plus the tú present subjunctive. Affirmative and negative tú commands use different patterns. Any object pronoun goes before the verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use no plus the tú present subjunctive. Affirmative and negative tú commands use different patterns. Any object pronoun goes before the verb.

lessons.title: Usted / ustedes commands · independent practice
lessons.objective: Usted / ustedes commands · independent practice: Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands.

words.es: El sábado visitaremos a nuestros primos.
words.en: On Saturday we will visit our cousins.

words.es: Vamos a salir temprano porque ya tenemos los boletos.
words.en: We are going to leave early because we already have the tickets.

words.es: Según el pronóstico, lloverá por la tarde.
words.en: According to the forecast, it will rain in the afternoon.
We will have to take umbrellas.
What will we do if they close the park?

words.es: Buscaremos un museo cerca del centro.
words.en: We will look for a museum near downtown.

words.es: Mis primos dijeron que el museo les parecía buena idea.
words.en: My cousins said that the museum seemed like a good idea to them.

words.es: Yo ya había buscado el horario de entrada.
words.en: I had already looked up the entrance hours.

lessons.speaking: Use Usted / ustedes commands while discussing plan around an uncertain forecast. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing plan around an uncertain forecast. Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands. No creates a negative command with the same verb form. Both addressees are practiced. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands. No creates a negative command with the same verb form. Both addressees are practiced.

lessons.title: Present progressive · independent practice
lessons.objective: Present progressive · independent practice: Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress.

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

words.es: La recepcionista encontró una habitación que daba al patio.
words.en: The receptionist found a room that faced the courtyard.

words.es: Nos explicó que costaría un poco más.
words.en: She explained that it would cost a little more.

lessons.speaking: Use Present progressive while discussing make a polite request and confirm it. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing make a polite request and confirm it. Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress. Leer uses leyendo; dormir uses durmiendo; pedir uses pidiendo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress. Leer uses leyendo; dormir uses durmiendo; pedir uses pidiendo.

lessons.title: Present perfect · independent practice
lessons.objective: Present perfect · independent practice: Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle.

words.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
words.en: I have opened the meeting room.

words.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
words.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

words.es: El director ha dicho que llegará a las diez.
words.en: The director has said that he will arrive at ten.
Have you seen the new document?

words.es: Sí, y hemos hecho una copia para cada persona.
words.en: Yes, and we have made a copy for each person.

words.es: Cuando llegó el director, todos estábamos listos.
words.en: When the director arrived, we were all ready.

words.es: Él preguntó quién había preparado el resumen.
words.en: He asked who had prepared the summary.

lessons.speaking: Use Present perfect while discussing report what has already been done. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing report what has already been done. Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle. Regular participles end in -ado or -ido; learn the listed irregular ones. Regional use versus the preterite varies. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle. Regular participles end in -ado or -ido; learn the listed irregular ones. Regional use versus the preterite varies.

lessons.title: Pluperfect: earlier past · independent practice
lessons.objective: Pluperfect: earlier past · independent practice: Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point.

words.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
words.en: Come to my house at nine.

words.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
words.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

words.es: Pon los libros junto a la puerta.
words.en: Put the books next to the door.

words.es: Haz una lista de las cosas frágiles.
words.en: Make a list of the fragile things.

words.es: Después llama a Julia y dile que ya estamos listos.
words.en: Then call Julia and tell her that we are ready.

words.es: Mi amiga llegó antes que los demás.
words.en: My friend arrived before the others.

words.es: Le mostré dónde estaban las cosas más delicadas.
words.en: I showed her where the most delicate things were.

lessons.speaking: Use Pluperfect: earlier past while discussing teach a task with commands. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing teach a task with commands. Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point.

lessons.title: Conditional perfect · independent practice
lessons.objective: Conditional perfect · independent practice: Use habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían plus an invariant participle for a hypothetical completed action.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.
Do not touch the works of art.

words.es: Si vienen en grupo, esperen junto a la escalera.
words.en: If you come as a group, wait next to the stairs.

words.es: Pregunten al personal si necesitan ayuda.
words.en: Ask the staff if you need help.

words.es: Una visitante preguntó dónde podía dejar el cochecito.
words.en: A visitor asked where she could leave the stroller.

words.es: El empleado le indicó un espacio junto a la recepción.
words.en: The employee pointed out a space next to reception.

lessons.speaking: Use Conditional perfect while discussing give formal directions clearly. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing give formal directions clearly. Use habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían plus an invariant participle for a hypothetical completed action. A counterfactual si clause needs the appropriate past subjunctive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían plus an invariant participle for a hypothetical completed action. A counterfactual si clause needs the appropriate past subjunctive.

lessons.title: Regular -ar present · independent practice
lessons.objective: Regular -ar present · independent practice: Remove -ar; add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an.

words.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
words.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

words.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
words.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

words.es: Mi madre quiere visitar el mercado.
words.en: My mother wants to visit the market.

words.es: Mi padre prefiere que salgamos temprano.
words.en: My father prefers us to leave early.

words.es: Deseo que todos tengan tiempo para descansar.
words.en: I wish everyone had time to rest.

words.es: Yo quiero preparar una cena en casa.
words.en: I want to prepare dinner at home.

words.es: Mis padres me preguntaron qué quería hacer primero.
words.en: My parents asked me what I wanted to do first.

words.es: Yo quería caminar sin un horario fijo.
words.en: I wanted to walk without a fixed schedule.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -ar present while discussing express wishes without changing subjects. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing express wishes without changing subjects. Remove -ar; add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Use the present for habits and current facts. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Remove -ar; add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Use the present for habits and current facts.

lessons.title: Regular -er present · independent practice
lessons.objective: Regular -er present · independent practice: Remove -er; add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en.

words.es: Creo que la biblioteca abre el sábado.
words.en: I think the library opens on Saturday.

words.es: No creo que cierre tan temprano.
words.en: I do not think it closes so early.

words.es: Dudo que ese anuncio sea reciente.
words.en: I doubt that that notice is recent.

words.es: Es posible que hayan cambiado el horario.
words.en: It is possible that they have changed the schedule.

words.es: Sabemos que el sitio web tiene un número de teléfono.
words.en: We know that the website has a phone number.
Let us call to confirm the information.

words.es: La persona que atendió confirmó que el aviso era antiguo.
words.en: The person who answered confirmed that the notice was old.

words.es: Nos dijo que la biblioteca cerraba una hora más tarde.
words.en: She told us that the library closed an hour later.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -er present while discussing check a doubtful claim with evidence. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing check a doubtful claim with evidence. Remove -er; add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en. Notice nosotros ends in -emos. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Remove -er; add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en. Notice nosotros ends in -emos.
